criteria.rationale: The exact checkout environment marker and pidfd handling are verified. L1/L2 are disclosed limits; L3 leaves an unresolved assumption that an unreadable same-user process is unrelated, although it could be a reviewer child and the run can still conclude.
The run record reports ended PIDs and the number of same-user processes whose environments could not be inspected.
The new record format remains compatible, but an incomplete reservation left without a marker by the previous ordering remains blocked and cannot be discovered or released by the new CLI path.

D1 addresses children that escape the adapter group by matching the run checkout and pinning the signal target; D2 records a failed run and receipt only after the marker proves its owner dead. L3 remains capable of bypassing cleanup. The design assessment found no structural deltas, so there are no mappings.
I checked the English and pt-BR manuals and scaffold copies: they state the Linux limit, describe the new lifecycle, and retain the prior template versions.
The new incomplete-receipt message directs users to find a stalled row with delegate ls, but that projection omits a legacy reservation with no marker.
The reviewed implementation, lifecycle records, brief and manuals fit the capability's approved areas; the structural assessment reports no deltas.

A per-run environment scan with pidfd signaling is a small sufficient addition because process-group cleanup misses own-session children; a generic supervisor is unnecessary. The choice is invalid when the scan cannot inspect a same-user process and still permits conclusion.

findings.action: A markerless reservation left by the earlier reserve-before-marker protocol is invisible to ListDelegationAttempts, while reviewAttemptAdmission still rejects its missing receipt. The new ordering prevents new cases but leaves the existing orphan state unrecoverable, so delegate ls/cancel cannot release it and later dispatches remain blocked.

When a same-user process environment is unreadable, the reaper returns its count without an error; dispatch only adds a limitation and leaves terminationFailed false. A run-owned child may therefore survive while cleanup and conclusion proceed, contrary to R1 and the constraint that unreclaimable runs stay unconcludable.

Release has no exclusive claim across the missing-receipt check, run write, and receipt write. Two concurrent cancels can both pass this check, write distinct failed runs, then race for the single receipt; the losing run remains recorded without a receipt and that cancel returns an error.

The R5/R6 release test constructs a reservation and dead-owner marker directly, then calls Store.ReleaseAbandonedAttempt. It does not interrupt a real dispatch between reservation and run recording or attempt a later dispatch, so the required R6 regression is absent.

Every receipt Lstat error other than not-exist is reported as 'it already has a receipt', including permission or I/O errors. The cancel diagnostic can give a false cause and does not expose the actionable filesystem error.
